title: How many angles of symmetry has a three-arm figure with unequal gaps?
description: A figure has three radial arms, but the gaps between the arms are not equal. A traced cutout of it is pinned at the centre and turned over the figure, and the turns that fit are looked for. Keeko's doubt is that three arms always give three angles of symmetry.
teaching_notes: One idea: with unequal gaps the arms cannot land on each other, so only the full turn fits. Watch for students who think the number of arms gives the number of angles.

source: A figure has 3 radial arms but the angles between the arms a
video_script.why: The child finds, with a cutout, that a three-arm figure with unequal gaps fits itself only after a full turn.
video_script.substitution: the book's three-arm figure with unequal gaps, traced and cut out
video_script.anchor: the book's figure with three radial arms and unequal gaps
video_script.wrong_answer: three arms give three angles of symmetry
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko counts the arms and says the figure has as many angles of symmetry as arms.

final_answer.value: Only 360°, so it has no rotational symmetry
final_answer.spoken: only three hundred sixty degrees, so it has no rotational symmetry

maths_rules: 3 radial arms with unequal gaps between them
trace the figure and cut out a copy; pin it at the centre and turn it over the figure
an arm that moves across a wide gap lands where a narrower gap lies, so the arms do not land on arms
the cutout fits only after the full turn of 360°
only 360° is an angle of symmetry, so there is no rotational symmetry
video_script.design: The three-arm figure with one wide gap and two narrower gaps. A traced cutout is pinned at the centre and turned, and it misses at every turn until the full turn. Keeko's doubt is that three arms mean three angles.

<bookmark mark='miss'/>It lands in a narrower gap, not on an arm.
The gaps are not equal, so the arms cannot land on each other.

beats.on_screen: Answer: Only 360°, so it has no rotational symmetry
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Only the full turn fits.
Three hundred sixty degrees is its only angle, so it has no rotational symmetry.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks three arms give three angles of symmetry.
<bookmark mark='third'/>Turn the cutout by one third of a full turn, and the arms miss their places.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The gaps are unequal, so three arms do not give three turns.
